marble.name: The Immune System
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Know that the body has an immune system that protects against illness: the skin acts as a barrier, white blood cells identify and destroy germs (bacteria and viruses), and vaccines train the immune system to recognise specific diseases before they cause illness
marble.prompt: Can you explain how their body fights off germs — and why getting a vaccine helps protect them from getting sick?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering how their amazing body works — learning about the heart, lungs, brain, skeleton, and five senses, plus understanding what their body needs to stay healthy and strong.

misconceptions: 'Medicine/antibiotics do the fighting' — rather than the body's OWN immune system doing the defending.
'Vaccines give you the disease' — they use weakened/inactive germs or pieces to train the body safely.
'Vaccines cure a disease you already have' — they prevent by training in advance, not treat after.
'Germs are all the same' — missing that bacteria and viruses are different kinds of invader.
'The skin is just a covering' — missing its role as the first line of defence (a barrier).
representations: Layered-defence diagram: skin barrier outside, white blood cells patrolling inside
White blood cell 'defender' finding and engulfing/destroying a germ
Vaccine-as-training: a harmless practice germ so the body learns to recognise the real one
A scab/cut-healing image for the barrier and its repair
Germ types (bacteria vs virus) as the invaders being defended against
authoredAnswer: The vaccine shows the immune system a harmless version (weakened, inactive, or just a piece) of the germ, so the white blood cells learn to recognise and 'remember' it — without the person getting ill, because the germ in the vaccine is too weak or inactive to cause disease. wrongAnswers.wrong: It works by giving you a small case of the disease so you get it and then it's over.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Says the vaccine infects you with the illness.
wrongAnswers.fix: Clarify the germ in the vaccine is weakened/inactive/a fragment — enough to be recognised, not enough to cause disease.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Attributes protection to the vaccine or medicine killing germs, not to training white blood cells.
wrongAnswers.fix: Shift agency to the immune system: the vaccine trains YOUR white blood cells; they do the recognising and destroying.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Says antibiotics kill viruses / cure colds.
wrongAnswers.fix: Distinguish bacteria (antibiotics can treat) from viruses (they can't); this is why prevention and the immune response matter.

wrongAnswers.wrong: You don't need germs — you get the illness just from being cold.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Names being cold, rather than germs, as the cause of illness.
wrongAnswers.fix: Establish germs (bacteria/viruses) as the cause of infectious illness; cold weather doesn't itself infect you.
